newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malbak busy after offer, unbundling near end.
newsitem.headline: Malbak busy after offer, unbundling near end.

text.p: Shares in Malbak Ltd, the South African industrial conglomerate in the process of unbundling, were active on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Wednesday on details of stock bids by a state finance body.

At the same time Malbak announced that the conditions needed to facilitate its unbundling had been fulfilled and the unpacking would go ahead as planned except for the cash payment and shares relating to Haggie Ltd.
The Public Investment Commissioners (PIC) on Tuesday detailed prices it is offering for shares unbundled from Malbak's distribution of its listed companies to shareholders.

"It is now known what the least price is you can get for the shares. Everyone has now gone and done their sums and worked out whether it is worth holding or selling the unbundled shares," a JSE dealer said.
By 1245 GMT over 1.18-million Malbak shares worth over 27 million rand had traded in 193 deals. The stocks were down 20 cents at 22.95 rand, moving off Tuesday's year high of 23.15.
"Out of the offer one can also see whether it is worth holding Malbak once the unbundling is finished and it is only a packaging company," the dealer said.

After the unbundling, Malbak sole assets will be a 68 percent stake in Kohler Ltd and 64 percent in U.K-based MY Holdings. Malbak's listing will be transferred to the JSE's packaging sector next Tuesday.

The PIC, which raises funds for government in South Africa's financial markets and runs the state's pension funds, has offered to buy the shares to gain footholds in local blue chip companies and prevent a flood of the shares onto the market which may depress share prices.

The state body will pay 27.65 rand a share for Ellerine Holdings Ltd shares, 29.40 rand for Foodcorp shares, 460 cents for New Clicks Holdings Ltd shares, 37.55 rand for SA Druggists Ltd shares and 715 cents per "new" unbundled Malbak share.

The cash offers are lower than market prices at the close of business on Tuesday, but compare well with the five day weighted averages for the stocks. Shareholders will not be charged brokerage fees, which could cost up to 1.5 percent of the total, the PIC said.

Malbak shareholders who do not sell their shares and are registered on April 25 will receive 13.950 Ellerine shares, 11.216 Foodcorp shares, 37.763 New Clicks shares and 16.490 SA Druggists stocks plus 75 rand for every 100 Malbak shares held.
Shareholders will be paid distributions on April 30.
